title: Bring a storage shelf under its sprinkler clearance line
instruction: Fire code: nothing stored here may stand taller than the red band on the white post, 11.5 cm above the table. Fix every item that breaks this rule; you may use the grey floor pads. Everything must end upright on the shelf or on a pad, not stacked.
context: Fire codes keep stored goods a set distance below sprinkler heads (18 in under the deflectors in NFPA 13 and OSHA 1910.159(c)(10)) so the spray can reach a fire; the band is a scaled stand-in. Three items already break it: find and fix them without creating a new breach.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge. Shelf: solid grey-painted wood block, 10 x 48 x 5 cm tall, long side across the table, at x 21 to 31, y -24 to +24, screwed down. Post: white PVC rod, 2 cm diameter, 20 cm tall, standing at x 36, y 0, glued down, with a red vinyl tape band 1 cm wide whose lower edge is 11.5 cm above the table. Pads: two dark-grey rubber mats, 8 x 8 cm, 4 mm thick, taped down at x 13, y +17 and -17. Cartons: four painted cardboard cubes, 4.5 cm, weighted to 80 g, square to the table edges, all at x 26 on the shelf, three blue and one orange: a blue one at y +19 with the orange one squarely on top of it (top 14 cm above the table), a blue one at y +1, a blue one at y -10. Bottles: two green plastic bottles, 5 cm diameter, 10 cm tall with a flat cap, sand-weighted to 150 g, standing on the shelf at x 26, y +10 and -19 (tops 15 cm above the table). Nothing else on the table. The layout is exact: in simulation run with -E object_jitter=0, because jitter can topple the stack.
scoring: At the end of the run, open both grippers, then measure with a tape measure. An item is stored if it stands upright (a bottle on its base, tilted 15 degrees or less, i.e. the centre of its top within 2.7 cm sideways of the centre of its base; a carton on any face, within 15 degrees), its centre is over the shelf or a pad, its underside is within 1 cm of that surface, its top is no higher than 11.5 cm above the table, and it is not stacked: not on another item, nothing on it. Score 0 if any item has left the table. Otherwise score = (A / 3) x (B / 3): A counts the three items that start too tall (the orange carton and both bottles) that are stored; B counts the three blue cartons that are stored. A bottle moved elsewhere on the shelf is still too tall; one laid down is not upright. Possible scores: 0, 1/9, 2/9, 1/3, 4/9, 2/3, 1.0. Only where items end up is judged: an item slid onto a pad, or the orange carton knocked off the stack that lands upright on the shelf, counts as stored, because it then meets the clearance rule. An orange carton knocked onto the table is not stored, but it frees the blue carton under it.
reset_notes: Mark each item's spot before the first trial. Between trials, stand the bottles at x 26 cm, y +10 and -19, the blue cartons at x 26 cm, y +1, -10 and +19, and set the orange carton squarely on the blue one at y +19. The shelf, post and pads stay put.
fidelity: Approximate. Cartons and bottles are rigid boxes and cylinders with default friction. The shelf, post and pads are fixed boxes and cylinders; the band is a short red cylinder around the post. The sim scores the final step without opening the grippers, so an item still held more than 1 cm above every support counts as not stored: unfixed if it started too tall, a new breach if it did not.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (Raised the left arm and reached the right arm toward a pad, bottles stayed on shelf); demo: 1.0 (Moved both bottles onto the pads and set the orange carton flat on the shelf)
